reason: Start with the stem-cell lineage to build toward living bone.
expectation: The signalling environment will produce bone-lineage cells, though I don't know how mature they will be.

effect: The lineage produces matrix-making osteoblasts and embedded osteocytes, so I can now work toward supplied living bone.
reaction: The distinction between matrix-producing and embedded bone cells is useful.
reason: Add mineral to the collagen framework to build the strong bone structure.
expectation: The crystals will reinforce the collagen framework, producing mineralized arm bones; I expect cells and vessels will still need to be incorporated.

effect: The framework is mineralised, and the contrast clarifies how collagen and mineral contribute different mechanical properties. I still need to add living cells and a blood supply.
reason: Combine the bone cells with blood vessels to work toward living, supplied bones.
expectation: I expect a vascularised bone-cell component that can be joined to the mineralised framework, though the exact result is uncertain.

reaction: The distinction between vessels and the tiny nutrient channels is useful.
reason: Join the supplied cells to the mineralised framework to complete the living bones.
expectation: I expect living arm bones containing mineralised matrix, bone cells and vessels.

reaction: The repeated nutrient-channel picture reinforces the blood supply, though it adds little to the previous result.
reason: Line the fibrous sleeve to complete the joint capsule.
expectation: The synovial membrane will line the sleeve and contribute slippery fluid without covering the cartilage surfaces.

alternatives.reason: Cartilage should also help form the joint, but I want to prepare the capsule first.

reaction: The lining and its contribution to joint fluid are clear.
reason: Add cartilage to the bones as the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect cartilage caps on the joint surfaces; the capsule and ligaments may still need to be added.

effect: The facing elbow surfaces now have cartilage caps, ready to be enclosed by the capsule.
reaction: The sliding-surface inset makes the cartilage's role clear.
reason: Join the capped bones to the capsule; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect a fluid-lined elbow joint, with ligaments possibly still needed for support.

effect: The capsule now encloses the cartilage-covered bone ends, with fluid helping the surfaces glide; ligaments remain to support the joint.
reaction: The connection between the lining, fluid and sliding surfaces is clear.
reason: Add the ligaments for support; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect a supported, movable elbow joint with ligaments spanning its sides.

effect: The ligaments complete the movable arm skeleton, supporting bending while resisting sideways movement; all chapter goals are complete.
reaction: The contrasting movement arrows make the ligaments' role clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Mineralising the collagen framework was most worthwhile: the planned inset connects collagen's toughness and mineral's resistance to compression to bone structure.

leastWorthwhile.text: Joining the supplied cells to the framework repeated the nutrient-channel picture from the preceding result and added little explanation.

surprise.text: The bone-cell supply picture clarified that nutrients reach embedded osteocytes through tiny fluid-filled channels, while red blood cells stay inside vessels.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though combining bone cells with blood vessels before adding them to the framework felt like an abstract construction rather than a literal developmental sequence.

continue.text: I would continue: the planned structural contrasts and joint cutaways make the biology interesting, although the last few choices were predictable.
